moves.text: I would let Douglas demand my authorization, then hand him the rehearsal ledger: authorship, influence, and permission are three separate empty chairs. He may occupy the first historically, influence the second imaginatively, but the third remains unfilled until a documented rights holder clears the proposed use.

I would make Leonardo pitch four increasingly lavish adaptations while I interrupt each with the same question: who authorized this? Douglas becomes both advocate and witness, forced to admit that creative excitement can forecast a work without granting anyone permission to make it.

I would place the Space receipt on the microphone as the scene’s only hard evidence: access_blocked, one read attempt, zero bytes, unknown cost, no request ID. Everyone must speak around that object without turning its missing audio or transcript into convenient dialogue.

I would have Douglas announce that he cannot authorize anything, then leave a long silence. Leonardo wants to fill it with adaptation; I let the silence expose the difference between an author’s presence, a character’s claim, and actual legal clearance.
